subject: It must be something simple I'm missing

messages.author: cab31ecf29fa17ff
messages.subject: It must be something simple I'm missing
parts:
Hi folks,

Any idea what might be going wrong? I’m using secr 4.4.7

groups.fit works but groups.time.fit gives me the error in red. Same input files. Ideally I want D to vary by group and time.

 

groups.fit <- secr.fit(capthist = IA, mask = mask.clipped,

                              model = list(D ~ g, lambda0 ~ g, sigma ~ g),

                              group = "Sex", detectfn = 14)

 

> groups.time.fit <- secr.fit(capthist = IA, mask = mask.clipped,

+                        model = list(D ~ t, lambda0 ~ g, sigma ~ g),

+                        group = "Sex", detectfn = 14)

Checking data

Preparing detection design matrices

Preparing density design matrix

Error in if (nrow(temp) < n) rbind(temp, temp[rep(1, n - nrow(df)), ,  :

  argument is of length zero

 

Inputs 6 sessions and a mask

IA<-read.capthist(captfile="2018_2021SEP_IA_SECR_capturedata.txt",

                  trapfile = list("2018_IA_SECR_traplocs_BLinterferenceremoved.txt",

                                  "2019MAY_IA_SECR_traplocs_BLinterferenceremoved.txt",

                                  "2019AUG_IA_SECR_traplocs_BLinterferenceremoved.txt",

                                  "2020SEP_IA_SECR_traplocs_BLinterferenceremoved.txt",

                                  "2021MAY_IA_SECR_traplocs_BLinterferenceremoved.txt",

                                  "2021SEP_IA_SECR_traplocs_BLinterferenceremoved.txt"),

                  detector = "multi",

                  fmt=c("trapID","XY"),

                  covnames=list("Sex"))

intervals(IA)<-c(12,3,13,8,4)/12

 

mask.clipped = make.mask(traps=traps(IA),#using final mask only as encompasses whole pen

          buffer=4*150,

          spacing=0.5*150,

          poly=fence,

          poly.habitat = TRUE)

 

Thanks,

Cheryl

messages.subject: Re: It must be something simple I'm missing
parts:
Cheryl
I think you may be applying 'openCR' thinking in 'secr', which doesn't always work. In openCR 't' is a synonym of (primary) 'session'. In secr, 't' refers to occasions within a (primary) session (secondary sessions in Pollock terminology), and you cannot model density as varying within a (primary) session (it's closed i.e. constant).

All I'm saying is that it may work if you use D~session instead of D~t.

I'd love to know if you've really found a bug in 4.4.7. I have been working on a significant bug for Poisson count data that Ian Durbach turned up today, and expect to put out a patched version in a couple of days.
Murray
